correctness.rationale: The eight-dimensional normal form with basis (x,y,a,b,c,d,e,f) and eleven nonzero multiplication products satisfies the commutative Jacobi identity and spans the free object by reduction of all degree-five monomials; in characteristics not 2,3 the explicit faithful model proves independence. A nonzero linear component of z is the image of x under an automorphism inducing an invertible graded generator change, so L_z has rank 5. For z in F², the degree-three map from (x,y) is M(A,B,C)=[[-B/2,A],[C,-B/2]], determinant (B²−4AC)/4. Nonzero quadratic part has an independent quartic output, giving rank 1+rank M, i.e. 2 on the nonzero quadric and 3 off it; cubic-only gives rank1 and quartic-only gives rank0. The discriminant rank-one symmetric cone has q²−1 nonzero finite-field points and unique singular vertex, so counts are q, q(q²−1), q³(q²−1), q^5(q−1), q^6(q²−1), and rank4 never occurs. Independently reconstructed all multiplication matrices over F5, obtaining 5,120,3000,12500,375000 for ranks 0,1,2,3,5 among 5^8 states. General assertions rest on the algebraic proof, not this sample.

value.rationale: Left-multiplication rank and annihilator dimension are intrinsic to a finite-dimensional algebra, and the free two-generated Jacobi–Jordan algebra is the canonical finite example with a known eight-dimensional normal form. The exact geometric rank loci, discriminant cone, forbidden rank four, and all-q arithmetic strata form a natural complete invariant rather than an arbitrary slice, and can support study of representations, generic rank and annihilator stratification.

limitations: Only free nonunital two-generated Jacobi–Jordan algebra over char not 2,3, rather than every JJ algebra.
